title: Plant Growth and Mineral Nutrition
subject: Biology

nodes.title: Plant Growth: Phases, Growth Curves & Mathematical Models
points: Growth: Irreversible, permanent increase in size, volume, or dry mass of an organism accompanied by metabolic processes.

Phases of growth: 1) Meristematic (cell division, dense cytoplasm, large nuclei, thin cellulosic walls); 2) Elongation (vacuolation, cell enlargement, new wall deposition); 3) Maturation / Differentiation (structural and functional specialization).
Arithmetic Growth: Only one daughter cell divides, the other differentiates. Linear graph: L_t = L₀ + rt.

Geometric Growth: Both daughter cells divide repeatedly. Sigmoid (S-shaped) curve: Lag phase (initial slow) → Log / Exponential phase (rapid maximal) → Stationary phase (nutrient limitation). Equation: W₁ = W₀ e^(rt).
Relative Growth Rate (r / Efficiency index): Capacity of plant to produce new material per unit time.

formulas.label: Arithmetic growth linear equation
formulas.expr: L_t = L₀ + rt (where L_t = length at time t, L₀ = initial length, r = growth rate)

formulas.label: Geometric growth exponential equation
formulas.expr: W₁ = W₀ e^(rt) (where W₁ = final size, W₀ = initial size, r = relative growth rate, t = time)

formulas.label: Sigmoid growth curve phases
formulas.expr: Lag phase (slow start) → Log / Exponential phase (rapid maximal) → Stationary phase (nutrient limitation)

nodes.title: Plant Growth Regulators: Auxins
points: Discovery: Charles Darwin & Francis Darwin observed canary grass coleoptile phototropism; F.W. Went isolated Auxin from oat (Avena sativa) coleoptile tips using agar blocks (Avena curvature test).
Precursor: Tryptophan (amino acid requiring Zn²⁺ cofactor).
Natural Auxins: IAA (Indole-3-acetic acid), IBA (Indole-3-butyric acid); Synthetic Auxins: NAA (Naphthalene acetic acid), 2,4-D (2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid).

Physiological roles & applications: 1) Apical Dominance: Growing apical bud inhibits growth of lateral axillary buds; decapitation promotes bushy growth (tea pruning, hedges); 2) Root initiation in stem cuttings; 3) Prevents premature fruit/leaf drop; 4) Selective weedicide: 2,4-D kills broad-leaved dicot weeds without harming monocot crops; 5) Induces Parthenocarpy in tomatoes.

formulas.label: Auxin bioassay & precursor
formulas.expr: Bioassay: Avena curvature test (F.W. Went) | Precursor: Tryptophan (Zn²⁺ cofactor)

formulas.label: 2,4-D selective weedicide application
formulas.expr: 2,4-D kills broad-leaved Dicot weeds (spares monocot cereal crops)

nodes.title: Gibberellins & Cytokinins
points: 1. Gibberellins: Discovered by E. Kurosawa in rice infected with fungus Gibberella fujikuroi ('Bakanae' foolish seedling disease). Most extensively studied is GA₃. Precursor: Mevalonic acid / Terpenes.

Physiological effects of GA: Bolting (rapid internodal elongation in rosette plants like cabbage, beet before flowering); elongates grape stalks; increases sugarcane stem length (boosts yield by up to 20 tons/acre); breaks seed dormancy by activating α-amylase to mobilize starch.
2. Cytokinins: Discovered by Skoog & Miller (Kinetin from herring sperm DNA). Letham isolated Zeatin from corn kernels (Zea mays). Precursor: Adenine (purine).

Physiological effects of Cytokinins: Promotes cell division (cytokinesis); overcomes apical dominance; Richmond-Lang effect (delays leaf senescence by nutrient mobilization); Morphogenesis control: High Auxin/Cytokinin ratio → Root induction; High Cytokinin/Auxin ratio → Shoot induction.

formulas.label: Gibberellin bolting effect
formulas.expr: Rosette plants (Cabbage, Beet) + GA₃ → Dramatic internodal elongation & flowering (Bolting)

formulas.label: Organogenesis hormone balance (Skoog & Miller)
formulas.expr: High Auxin : Low Cytokinin → Root development | Low Auxin : High Cytokinin → Shoot development

formulas.label: Richmond-Lang effect
formulas.expr: Cytokinins delay senescence of leaves by preventing chlorophyll degradation and nutrient mobilization

nodes.title: Ethylene & Abscisic Acid (ABA - Stress Hormone)
points: 1. Ethylene (Gaseous Hormone): Discovered by H.H. Cousins (ripening oranges accelerate banana ripening). Precursor: Methionine. Commercial formulation: Ethephon.

Physiological effects of Ethylene: Accelerates fruit ripening (climacteric respiratory rise); induces horizontal growth of seedlings, axis swelling, and apical hook (triple response); promotes senescence and abscission of leaves/flowers; breaks seed dormancy; increases root hair surface area.
2. Abscisic Acid (ABA / Dormin / Stress Hormone): Discovered by Addicott (Abscisin II) and Wareing (Dormin). Precursor: Carotenoids / Mevalonic acid.

Physiological effects of ABA: General growth inhibitor; antitranspirant (stimulates rapid stomatal closure during water stress by K⁺ efflux); induces seed dormancy preventing vivipary; acts antagonistically to Gibberellins (ABA vs GA balance).

formulas.label: Ethylene precursor and ripening trigger
formulas.expr: Precursor: Methionine | Fruit ripening gas (causes climacteric respiratory rise)

formulas.label: ABA stress hormone action
formulas.expr: Water stress → ABA synthesis → K⁺ efflux from guard cells → Rapid stomatal closure

formulas.label: Antagonistic hormone pairs
formulas.expr: GA (breaks seed dormancy) vs ABA (induces seed dormancy) | Auxin (apical dominance) vs Cytokinin (bushy growth)

nodes.title: Photoperiodism & Vernalization
points: Photoperiodism (Garner & Allard, 1920 in Maryland Mammoth tobacco): Response of plants to relative day and night lengths for induction of flowering.

1. Short Day Plants (SDP / Long Night Plants): Flower when exposed to photoperiods shorter than critical photoperiod; require uninterrupted dark night (Tobacco, Soybean, Xanthium). A flash of light during night inhibits flowering!
2. Long Day Plants (LDP / Short Night Plants): Flower when photoperiod exceeds critical day length (Wheat, Radish, Spinach).
3. Day Neutral Plants (DNP): Flowering unaffected by day length (Tomato, Sunflower, Pea).

Phytochrome pigment (Borthwick & Hendricks): Photoreceptor interconverting between P_r (absorbs 660 nm red light, inactive) and P_fr (absorbs 730 nm far-red light, active form inducing flowering in LDP and inhibiting SDP).
Vernalization (Lysenko): Promotion of flowering by low-temperature cold treatment (1-5 °C e.g. winter cereals, biennial crops like cabbage, carrot); mediated by hypothetical hormone Vernalin.

formulas.label: Phytochrome interconversion equilibrium
formulas.expr: P_r (660 nm red light) ⇌ P_fr (730 nm far-red light, biologically active form)

formulas.label: SDP vs LDP flowering triggers
formulas.expr: SDP: Requires uninterrupted dark night > critical duration | LDP: Requires light > critical duration

nodes.title: Mineral Nutrition: Criteria of Essentiality & Classification
points: Criteria of Essentiality (Arnon & Stout, 1939): 1) Plant cannot complete life cycle without the element; 2) Requirement is specific and cannot be replaced by another element; 3) Element is directly involved in plant metabolism.
17 Essential Elements:
- Macronutrients (> 10 mmol/kg dry matter): C, H, O (framework elements from CO₂/H₂O); N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S.
- Micronutrients / Trace elements (< 10 mmol/kg dry matter): Fe, Mn, Cu, Zn, B, Mo, Cl, Ni.

Functional roles: Structural (C, H, O, N); Energy-related (Mg in chlorophyll, P in ATP); Enzyme activators (Mg²⁺ activates Rubisco & PEPcase; Zn²⁺ activates alcohol dehydrogenase; Mo activates nitrogenase); Osmotic regulators (K⁺ controls stomatal opening and ionic balance).

formulas.label: Macronutrients mnemonic (9 elements)
formulas.expr: C, H, O, N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S ('CHON PK Ca Mg S')

formulas.label: Micronutrients mnemonic (8 elements)
formulas.expr: Fe, Mn, Zn, Cu, B, Mo, Cl, Ni

formulas.label: Enzyme cofactors matching
formulas.expr: Rubisco & PEPcase = Mg²⁺ | Alcohol dehydrogenase = Zn²⁺ | Nitrogenase = Mo & Fe

nodes.title: Specific Roles of Minerals & Deficiency Symptoms
points: Nitrogen (N): Nucleic acids, proteins, chlorophyll; deficiency causes chlorosis in older leaves first (mobile).
Phosphorus (P): ATP, phospholipids; deficiency causes purple/red pigmentation on leaves, stunted root growth.
Potassium (K): K⁺/Na⁺ balance, stomatal regulation, protein synthesis; deficiency causes marginal leaf scorch / necrosis.
Calcium (Ca): Constituent of middle lamella (Calcium pectate), mitotic spindle; IMMOBILE, deficiency causes necrosis of young meristem tips (Blossom-end rot of tomato).
Magnesium (Mg): Central atom of chlorophyll porphyrin ring; activates Rubisco; deficiency causes interveinal chlorosis in older leaves.
Zinc (Zn): Auxin (IAA) biosynthesis; deficiency causes 'little leaf' disease and khaira disease of rice.
Boron (B): Pollen tube germination, sugar translocation; deficiency causes brown heart rot in turnip/beet, death of shoot tip.
Manganese (Mn): Photolysis of water in Photosystem II (with Cl⁻, Ca²⁺); deficiency causes marsh spot in peas.
Molybdenum (Mo): Component of nitrogenase; deficiency causes 'whiptail' disease of cauliflower.

formulas.label: Key deficiency disease signatures
formulas.expr: Ca = Blossom-end rot | Zn = Little leaf, Khaira of rice | B = Brown heart rot | Mo = Whiptail of cauliflower

formulas.label: Photolysis of water catalysts
formulas.expr: 2H₂O (Light, Mn²⁺, Cl⁻, Ca²⁺) → 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ + O₂↑

nodes.title: Nitrogen Metabolism: Biological Nitrogen Fixation
points: Nitrogen Cycle: Ammonification (decaying proteins → NH₃ by Bacillus ramosus), Nitrification, Denitrification (NO₃⁻ → N₂ gas by Pseudomonas & Thiobacillus).
Nitrification (two-step chemoautotrophic oxidation): 1) 2NH₃ + 3O₂ (Nitrosomonas / Nitrosococcus) → 2NO₂⁻ + 2H⁺ + 2H₂O; 2) 2NO₂⁻ + O₂ (Nitrobacter) → 2NO₃⁻.

Biological Nitrogen Fixation (BNF): Free-living aerobic (Azotobacter, Beijerinckia); Anaerobic (Clostridium); Cyanobacteria (Anabaena, Nostoc in heterocysts); Symbiotic (Rhizobium in legumes, Frankia in non-legume Alnus).
Nitrogenase Enzyme Complex: Mo-Fe protein; poisoned by O₂. Protected by Leghemoglobin (pink oxygen scavenger in root nodules creating anaerobic niche).
Energetics: Requires 16 ATP to fix 1 molecule of N₂ into 2 molecules of NH₃ (8 ATP per NH₃ produced!).

formulas.label: Biological nitrogen fixation equation
formulas.expr: N₂ + 8e⁻ + 8H⁺ + 16ATP (Nitrogenase) → 2NH₃ + H₂ + 16ADP + 16Pi

formulas.label: ATP cost per ammonia molecule
formulas.expr: 16 ATP / 2 NH₃ = 8 ATP required per NH₃ produced

formulas.label: Nitrification two-step reactions
formulas.expr: NH₃ → NO₂⁻ (Nitrosomonas) → NO₃⁻ (Nitrobacter)

nodes.title: High-Weightage Board Questions & Hormone Functions
points: Board Q1: State the discovery, physiological effects, and agricultural applications of: 1) Auxins (apical dominance, 2,4-D weedicide); 2) Gibberellins (bolting, sugarcane yield increase); 3) Ethylene (fruit ripening).
Board Q2: Describe the criteria of essentiality of mineral elements proposed by Arnon and Stout.
Board Q3: Explain the role of Leghemoglobin and Nitrogenase in root nodule nitrogen fixation.
Board Q4: Define Photoperiodism and differentiate between Short Day Plants and Long Day Plants.
Board Q5: Describe the Richmond-Lang effect of cytokinins and Avena curvature test for auxins.

formulas.label: Agricultural applications summary
formulas.expr: 2,4-D = Dicot weedicide | GA₃ = Elongates sugarcane stems & grape pedicels | Ethylene = Ripens bananas & tomatoes

formulas.label: Leghemoglobin function
formulas.expr: Acts as an oxygen scavenger to create anaerobic microenvironment for O₂-sensitive Nitrogenase

nodes.title: MHT-CET & NEET High-Speed Shortcuts & Traps
points: TRAP 1: Mobile vs Immobile nutrient deficiency symptoms: Deficiency of MOBILE elements (N, P, K, Mg) appears in OLDER leaves first. Deficiency of IMMOBILE elements (Ca, S, Fe) appears in YOUNGER leaves first!
TRAP 2: Hormone precursors: Auxin = Tryptophan (needs Zn²⁺); Ethylene = Methionine; Cytokinin = Adenine (purine); GA & ABA = Mevalonic acid / Terpenes.
TRAP 3: Sugarcane spraying with GA₃ increases stem length and boosts yield by up to 20 tons per acre.
TRAP 4: Energy cost of nitrogen fixation: 16 ATP per N₂ (8 ATP per NH₃).
TRAP 5: Denitrifying bacteria: Pseudomonas denitrificans and Thiobacillus denitrificans convert soil nitrates into atmospheric N₂.

formulas.label: Nutrient mobility deficiency location mnemonic
formulas.expr: Mobile (N, P, K, Mg) = Older leaves first | Immobile (Ca, S, Fe) = Younger leaves first

formulas.label: Hormone precursors checklist
formulas.expr: Auxin = Tryptophan | Ethylene = Methionine | Cytokinin = Adenine (purine) | GA & ABA = Mevalonic acid / Terpenes

formulas.label: Denitrification reaction
formulas.expr: 2NO₃⁻ → 2NO₂⁻ → 2NO → N₂O → N₂↑ (Pseudomonas & Thiobacillus)
